questions.answer: The slits are illuminated by the same incident wavefront, so the emerging waves have a constant phase difference and are coherent. Alternating bright and dark fringes are observed.
accepted_alternatives: Same source gives the two slit waves the same frequency and a constant phase difference; a stable bright-dark fringe pattern forms.

parts.answer: The same absolute endpoint-reading uncertainty is spread across several fringe intervals, so dividing the longer span reduces the percentage uncertainty in one spacing.
accepted_alternatives: A longer measured distance gives a smaller fractional uncertainty than a single narrow fringe spacing.
